label: Canva
blurb: Make clean thumbnails, logos, and promo art in your browser, then export them for your Horizon world.

lessons.title: What Is Canva?
lessons.subtitle: Your online design studio
steps: Canva is a free web app for making images, logos, and video in your browser.
Open canva.com and sign in. Nothing to install - it runs on any computer.
The home screen has a big search bar and a purple 'Create a design' button.
Your past work sits under 'Projects' in the left menu. Click one to reopen it.
Some tools and templates show a crown - those need a paid Canva Pro plan.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Canva runs in a web browser. You do not need to download anything.

quiz.q: What do you need to install to use Canva?

lessons.title: Start a New Design
lessons.subtitle: Pick a template or set your own size
steps: Click 'Create a design' at the top right of the home screen.
Pick a ready size like 'Logo', 'Poster', or 'Instagram Post' from the list.
Or choose 'Custom size' and type a width and height in pixels (px).
For game art, pixels (px) is the right unit. 1280 x 720 is a safe start.
The blank or template design opens in the editor, ready to change.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Use px for screen and game art. Use inches or cm only when printing.

quiz.q: Which unit fits game and screen art?

lessons.title: The Editor Layout
lessons.subtitle: Left panel, canvas, top bar
steps: The left-side panel holds your tools: Design, Elements, Text, Uploads, more.
The big white page in the middle is the canvas - your design.
The top toolbar changes to match whatever you have selected.
Top right has the 'Share' and 'Download' buttons for when you finish.
The bottom bar shows pages, zoom level, and the add-page button.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Click empty space to see fewer buttons. Click an item to see its tools.

quiz.q: Where do the tools like Text and Elements live?

lessons.title: Pick a Template
lessons.subtitle: Start from a ready-made design
steps: Open the 'Design' tab on the left, or search at the top of the panel.
Type what you want, like 'game logo' or 'thumbnail', and press Enter.
Click a template you like - it drops onto your page right away.
Templates with a crown need Canva Pro. Plenty are free - look for those.
Now change the text, colors, and photos to make it your own.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: A template is only a start. Swap every word and color so it feels like yours.

quiz.q: What does clicking a template do?

lessons.title: Add and Edit Text
lessons.subtitle: Fonts, size, color, and bold
steps: Click the 'Text' tab, then 'Add a text box', or pick a heading style.
Double-click the box and type your words.
With text selected, use the top toolbar to pick a font and a size.
Click the color tile to recolor the text. Click 'B' to make it bold.
Drag the round corner handles to resize the whole text box.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Fewer words, bigger font. Big bold text is easier to read at a glance.

quiz.q: Which button makes text bold?

lessons.title: Text Effects
lessons.subtitle: Shadow, outline, and curve
steps: Select a text box so the top toolbar shows text tools.
Click 'Effects' to open the style choices on the left.
'Shadow' adds depth. 'Hollow' gives an outline. 'Lift' floats the text.
Click 'Curve' and drag the slider to bend the text along an arc.
Each effect has sliders to set how strong it looks.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: One effect is plenty. A shadow or outline makes text read on busy art.

quiz.q: Which effect bends text into an arc?

lessons.title: Upload Your Images
lessons.subtitle: Bring your own photos in
steps: Click the 'Uploads' tab on the left panel.
Press 'Upload files' and pick a photo from your computer.
Wait for it to appear in the Uploads grid.
Drag it onto the canvas, or click it to drop it on the page.
Drag the corner handles to size it. Canva saves uploads for next time.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Canva takes JPG, PNG, and SVG files. A clear, large photo always looks better.

quiz.q: Which tab holds files from your computer?

lessons.title: Elements and Shapes
lessons.subtitle: Shapes, lines, and stickers
steps: Open the 'Elements' tab to find shapes, lines, stickers, and graphics.
'Lines and Shapes' at the top adds a square, circle, or straight line.
Search a word like 'arrow' or 'star' to find a matching graphic.
Stickers are graphics that can move - search and click to add one.
Click any element to recolor or resize it with the top toolbar.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: A simple shape behind text makes a clean badge or button look.

quiz.q: Where do shapes and stickers live?

lessons.title: Photos, Frames and Grids
lessons.subtitle: Place photos and set a background
steps: Find stock photos under 'Elements' > 'Photos', or use your own uploads.
A 'Frame' is a shape that crops a photo - drag a photo into it to fill it.
A 'Grid' splits the page into photo slots - drop a photo into each one.
To set a page background, right-click a photo and pick 'Set as background'.
Frames and grids are under the 'Elements' tab, below Lines and Shapes.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Drop a photo onto a frame and it snaps to that shape, cropped and clean.

quiz.q: What does dropping a photo into a frame do?

lessons.title: Remove the Background
lessons.subtitle: Cut out a subject (Canva Pro)
steps: Click an image, then click 'Edit photo' in the top toolbar.
Choose 'BG Remover'. Canva erases the background in one click.
This tool needs Canva Pro. Free accounts do not have it.
Use it to lift a character or logo onto a clean, see-through area.
A cut-out subject looks great layered over other art.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Background removal plus a transparent PNG export gives a clean game sprite.

quiz.q: Which plan has the Background Remover?

lessons.title: Colors and the Picker
lessons.subtitle: Recolor and match any color
steps: Select an element, then click its color tile in the top toolbar.
Pick from document colors, default swatches, or add a new one.
Type a hex code like FF5500 to set an exact color.
Use the eyedropper to grab a color from somewhere else on your page.
Saved brand colors appear here too, but need Canva Pro.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Two or three colors is enough. Reuse the same ones so your design looks tidy.

quiz.q: What does the eyedropper do?

lessons.title: Arrange and Align
lessons.subtitle: Stacking order and lining up
steps: Click an item, then click 'Position' in the top toolbar.
The 'Arrange' tab sends an item forward or back in the stack.
'To front' puts it on top. 'To back' hides it behind everything.
The 'Align' part snaps items to the left, center, or middle of the page.
Select two or more items first to space them evenly.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Centered text and lined-up edges instantly make a design look professional.

quiz.q: Which button holds Arrange and Align?

lessons.title: Group, Lock and Copy
lessons.subtitle: Handy keys for objects
steps: Select two or more items and press Ctrl G to group them as one.
Press Ctrl Shift G to ungroup them again.
Press Ctrl D to duplicate the selected item.
Click the padlock icon to lock an item so it cannot move by accident.
The transparency icon fades an item from solid to see-through.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Group a logo's parts so they move together and never drift out of line.

quiz.q: Which keys group items together?

lessons.title: Make a Game Thumbnail
lessons.subtitle: Bold and readable when small
steps: Start a 1280 x 720 design - a common thumbnail and banner size.
Use few words in a big, bold font. Three or four words is plenty.
Pick high contrast: light text on a dark area, or dark on light.
Put one clear subject - a character or logo - as the focus.
Shrink the preview on screen. If you can still read it, it works.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Add a dark shadow or outline behind text so it reads on any background.

quiz.q: What makes a thumbnail easy to read small?

lessons.title: Animate and Export Video
lessons.subtitle: Add motion, save as MP4
steps: Select a page or an item, then click 'Animate' in the top toolbar.
Pick a motion like 'Rise', 'Pan', or 'Fade'.
Press the play button at the top to preview the movement.
To save motion, download as 'MP4 Video' or 'GIF', not a still image.
Add more pages to make a longer clip - each page is a scene.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: A little motion grabs attention. Keep it subtle so text stays easy to read.

quiz.q: Which export keeps the animation?

lessons.title: Download Your Design
lessons.subtitle: PNG, JPG, and transparent
steps: Click 'Share' at the top right, then 'Download'.
PNG is sharp and best for logos, text, and game art.
JPG makes a smaller file, good for photos but not for crisp edges.
Tick 'Transparent background' for a see-through PNG (needs Canva Pro).
Set the size. Bigger numbers mean a sharper, larger image file.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Use PNG for anything with text or sharp edges. JPG softens them.

quiz.q: Which format stays sharp for text and logos?

lessons.title: Organize and Share
lessons.subtitle: Folders, links, and teammates
steps: Open 'Projects' in the left menu to see every design you have made.
Make a folder and drag designs into it to keep work tidy.
Star a design to pin it to the top for quick access.
Click 'Share' to invite people by email or copy a link.
Set a link to 'can edit', 'can comment', or 'can view' before you send it.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Set a share link to 'can view' if you only want people to look, not change it.

quiz.q: What does a 'can view' share link allow?

lessons.title: Set Up a Brand Kit
lessons.subtitle: Save your look (Canva Pro)
steps: The Brand Kit stores your logo, colors, and fonts in one place. It needs Pro.
Open the 'Brand' tab and add your brand colors with their hex codes.
Upload your logo so you can drop it into any design fast.
Set brand fonts so every design uses the same style.
In the editor, your brand items show at the top of the color and font menus.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: A saved Brand Kit keeps every thumbnail and logo looking like the same creator.

quiz.q: What does a Brand Kit save?

lessons.title: Magic Resize
lessons.subtitle: One design, many sizes (Pro)
steps: Magic Resize reshapes a finished design to new sizes. It needs Canva Pro.
Click 'Resize' at the top left of the editor.
Pick target sizes, or type a custom width and height.
Choose 'Copy and resize' to keep the original and make new copies.
Check each copy - you may need to nudge text so it still fits.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Make the thumbnail once, then resize it for a banner and a square icon fast.

quiz.q: What does Magic Resize do?

lessons.title: Transparent Art for Horizon
lessons.subtitle: Export clear PNGs for panels
steps: Make your logo or icon with no background box behind it.
Download as PNG and tick 'Transparent background' (needs Canva Pro).
A clear PNG drops onto a Horizon panel with no ugly square around it.
Use power-of-two sizes like 512, 1024, or 2048 px for clean in-world textures.
Keep art simple and high-contrast so it reads on a panel from a distance.
lessons.tip: Pro tip: Transparent PNGs at 1024 x 1024 make crisp panel logos and badges in Horizon.

quiz.q: Which export suits Horizon panel art?
